chapter: Old bandleaders, drummers and Edgewater years
title: Jules Baduc, drummers, the Cotton Club and an audition for his own job
summary: Frank calls Jules Baduc the worst drummer on tempo, then recalls playing the Cotton Club and Bourbon Street and auditioning for his own job.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I played with Jews in the rave. I swear to God, I don't know how the hell he ever, he was the worst drummer I ever played with. I swear before God. Never could keep tempo. But he threw the sticks up in the air and he jigged and everything else. But he's still playing too. Oh yeah, he sure is. He's still there.
He's in Houston. He's in Houston.
Yeah, he's in Houston. When did you play with Ray? With Jules. You played with Jules? Yeah, I played with Jules.

I played there with that, what was that place on the highway, on Clavin Avenue up there? Remember that place? What the hell they called? We used to put some Jacks programs on up there. How far up was it? Not too far, it was past where, it was past the roadways. Oh, up in Jefferson. Yeah, yeah, up in Jefferson. Thomas C's joint. Thomas C was at our end.
Thomas C was over across the river. Huh? Evans Thomas C was across the river.
Now wait a minute, he was on this side.
Midway, Evans Thomas C was midway. Well, who had this place on this side of the river? From Napoleon Avenue Ferry. Huh?
No, this place on this side of the river, don't you know? They rented the cabins in the back there for...
Oh, I know what you were talking about.
Yeah, they're right across the street from where the Arrow Room used to be.
Cotton Club. Near the Cotton Club? Yeah, I think that was it, the Cotton Club. Sure, that was it. Not the Blue Horseshoe.

No, no, no. Cotton Club. No, the Cotton Club. Blue Horseshoe. Blue Horseshoe was backed by the... Yeah, that was it, the Cotton Club. Blue Horseshoe used to be backed by the Two Bits Club in the... What's in the... Where you were. And that was where Farzola used to go all the time. In fact, one morning we were playing the theme song, the WWL, and... I don't know whether it's just good to put on or not. He's leaving the... They're just playing the theme and Farz walks out of the studio and Ed Hernan says, where are you going? He says, I gotta go out the Blue Horseshoe. I remember that my girlfriend left her teeth on the windowsill. I gotta go pick him up.
You got the right name. Cotton Club, that's it.
Yeah, you were at the Cotton Club?
I was with Jules Baduc. Jules Baduc. Yeah, Jules. Ray was at that time was with Crosby, Bob Crosby. Jules had a very good band down there on Bourbon Street.

I worked with him down there where Jumbo's joint is today. I played with him down there and I made an audition for that job. And I was working in there with Ray McNamara. I think... And he come and got me to audition for a job. He said, do me a favor. Do me a favor. Do me a favor. He says, I want to make an audition for a guy. In fact, Joe Massara. When I went in there and made the place over there, we were hoisting in another place. And who walks in there is Joe Massara. I says, for Christ's sake, I'm working for the guy right now. I said... And I went and met to McNamara that night. I said, Ray, I said, I auditioned for my own job over here. He says, well, take it. He says, I ain't gonna stay in this place anyway. He says, I'm sick and tired of it.
